role: PIXL specialist (pixl-kit profile), review repair of the authoring-01 connected plan; no generation, no provider request, no state writes

conventions.lines: one-based inclusive file-local bounds; each cited range was opened and verified at build time to contain the wording relied on (see verification in specialist-report.json)
conventions.authority: PLAR labels requirement / proposal / observation / unknown, asserted by the specialist for the caller to compare; 'requirement' includes consumer-code behavior and adopted caller decisions where the basis says so
conventions.scope: whole asset/stage, 'seed rotation construction', 'this authoring branch', 'method', or 'example'
conventions.images: zero-based pixel coordinates; component boxes from pixl_asset_check are measurements, not verdicts

summary_of_substantive_corrections: transparent-exterior (working, retry, paused): review route corrected - deciding which pixels are 'the mark' and whether a plate/matte is unwanted is visual judgment; mechanical measurement kept only where it is decidable (seed-rotation alpha equality); blanket 'no plate' narrowed to unintended matte/tile.

working.q.frame-assembly: 'lossless copy' bounded to alpha + visible RGBA (transparent RGB insignificant); 'duplication' bounded to undocumented substitution; construction-scoped pixel-exact rotation clause added as a proposal (listed in the policy but carried by no Q record).

working.q.motion-continuity: required outcome (continuous, evenly paced loop, seamless wrap) separated from contract-bound expert clauses (anchor/volume) and construction-scoped clauses (cluster count, stepped phases, no morphing/near-hold).
working.q.activity-not-success: 'arrowhead' and 'pause bars' re-scoped as expert guidance derived from proposed motifs of other members; check mark / terminal pose remain required.

consumers (working, retry, paused) and delivery.q.destination: 'actual consumer renderer' named as the fixture; 'observed live 100 ms frame advance' corrected to what the fixture evidences (timeline frame indices incl. the 400 ms wrap plus observed cycling; wall-clock not measured); 1x/3x routes stated.
working.q.geometry: 'padding' defined as added canvas so in-cell transparent margins are not rejected; slicing attributed to renderer/view.mjs.

criteria.original_check: Decode the delivered PNG as exactly 64x16: four horizontal 16x16 cells at x=0,16,32,48 with no gutters, padding or extra canvas; the consumer slices frame*16,0,16,16 for frames=4 and advances at display.frameMs 100 ms per frame (nominal 400 ms cycle).

clauses.text: Decode the delivered PNG as exactly 64x16
clauses.basis: BRIEF line 3 (16x16 cells, four horizontal frames) with src/queue-view.ts running frames 4 and display.cell [16,16]; the renderer fixture draws nothing unless width == 16*frames and height == 16 and marks 'Wrong sheet size' otherwise (consumer code behavior).

clauses.text: four horizontal 16x16 cells at x=0,16,32,48
clauses.basis: Consumer code behavior: the fixture slices drawImage(frame*16, 0, 16, 16) (renderer/view.mjs line 38); authoring-plar image_geometry.

clauses.text: with no gutters, padding or extra canvas
clauses.basis: Gutters or extra canvas change the 64x16 geometry or shift cell content under frame*16 slicing (consumer code). 'Padding' is ambiguous: transparent margin inside a 16x16 cell is normal pixel-art composition and is not prohibited by any source; the join-result expectation 'no gutters, padding' in the rotation policy refers to added canvas between/around cells.

clauses.text: the consumer slices frame*16,0,16,16 for frames=4 and advances at display.frameMs 100 ms per frame
clauses.basis: Correct facts, wrong attribution: slicing and frame advance are implemented in the supplied renderer fixture renderer/view.mjs paint() (lines 30-41: floor(max(elapsed,0)/frameMs) % frames); src/queue-view.ts supplies frames 4 and frameMs 100 only. render.choice.destination records the engine as 'Supplied browser fixture executing actual queue modules'.

clauses.text: (nominal 400 ms cycle)
clauses.basis: Arithmetic from BRIEF 4 frames x 100 ms; authoring-plar animation requirement nominal_cycle_ms 400.

criteria.proposed_check: Decode the delivered PNG as exactly 64x16: four horizontal 16x16 cells at x=0,16,32,48 with no gutters or added canvas between or around the cells (transparent margin inside a cell is composition, not padding). Basis: src/queue-view.ts declares running frames 4, display.cell [16,16] and frameMs 100; the supplied renderer fixture renderer/view.mjs draws only when width == 16*frames and height == 16, slices frame*16,0,16,16 and advances floor(elapsed/100) mod 4 (nominal 400 ms cycle).
criteria.change_explanation: Old: 'no gutters, padding or extra canvas' and 'the consumer slices ...'. New: 'padding' defined as added canvas between/around cells so transparent in-cell margins are not rejected; slicing/advance attributed to the renderer fixture (renderer/view.mjs) with src/queue-view.ts supplying frames and frameMs. Geometry requirement unchanged.
criteria.discriminating_alternative: (1) A 68x16 sheet with 1-px transparent gutters (cells at x=0,17,34,51) still holds four 16x16 frames at 100 ms as the brief's prose says, but the fixture refuses it ('Wrong sheet size'): the literal check rejects it and the rejection is source-supported by consumer code. (2) A 64x16 sheet whose marks occupy 10x10 of each cell with 3-px transparent margins is brief-conforming; the original word 'padding' could be read to reject it, the clarified text cannot.

criteria.original_check: In every cell, all pixels outside the activity marks have alpha 0; no opaque matte, plate, grey tile or fringe in any frame (the rejected generated frame whose background held 193 opaque #808080 pixels is this failure class). Partial alpha on mark pixels is permitted; binary alpha is not required.

clauses.text: all pixels outside the activity marks (in every cell) have alpha 0
clauses.basis: BRIEF line 3 'transparent backgrounds'; authoring-plar background requirement (transparent; binary alpha not required). Which opaque pixels are 'the mark' is a visual judgment, except under the seed-rotation construction where the exterior is exactly the alpha-0 set of cw^k(seed) and is mechanically decidable.
clauses.scope: whole asset (outcome); mechanical form only under the seed-rotation construction

clauses.text: no opaque matte, plate, grey tile or fringe
clauses.basis: Unintended canvas matte / grey tile / fringe violates the transparent-background requirement (historical verdict evidence). 'Plate' as a blanket prohibition is an expert construction preference: the PIXL profile distinguishes an unintended canvas matte from a deliberate plate/badge/backing with transparent exterior, which the brief does not forbid.
clauses.scope: matte/tile/fringe: whole asset (requirement); 'no deliberate plate': expert proposal, scoped to this authoring branch's construction

clauses.text: (the rejected generated frame whose background held 193 opaque #808080 pixels is this failure class)
clauses.basis: Historical failure evidence retained in the store; it illustrates the failure class and does not define the rule.

clauses.text: Partial alpha on mark pixels is permitted; binary alpha is not required.
clauses.basis: Contract al=full; authoring-plar background requirement reason; caller style decision not_prescribed 'Binary alpha'. Non-restriction; keep.

criteria.proposed_check: Split into a measured part and a visual part. Measured (mechanical/local): retain every cell's alpha histogram and exact RGBA component boxes; no cell may contain an alpha>0 region that reaches all four cell edges or fills the cell (canvas matte / grey tile). Under the seed-rotation construction, each cell's alpha channel must equal that of cw^k(seed) (224 alpha-0 pixels per cell), which decides the exterior mechanically; RGB values of alpha-0 pixels are not significant. Visual (visual/visual): viewed at 1x and 3x on #172336, the exterior of every frame shows the panel with no unintended matte, tile, halo or fringe; a deliberate opaque backing shape is acceptable only when it is part of the mark's recorded design and the exterior stays transparent. The rejected frame with 193 opaque #808080 background pixels (live.working-animation-01.review.verdict.1) is the failure class. Partial alpha on mark pixels is permitted; binary alpha is not required.
criteria.proposed_domain: visual (if kept as one record); otherwise mechanical for the measured record and visual for the visual record
criteria.proposed_mode: visual (if kept as one record); otherwise local + visual
criteria.change_explanation: Old: one mechanical/local check that asks which pixels are 'outside the activity marks' and whether a 'plate' is present. New: the exterior decision is made mechanical only where it actually is (seed-rotation construction: alpha channel equals cw^k(seed)); otherwise the matte/plate/fringe judgment is routed to a visual review with saved native/enlarged views. 'No plate' is narrowed to unintended matte/tile; a deliberate recorded backing shape is not rejected. Transparent-RGB values are declared insignificant (AUTHORING-RESULT.json line 130 evidence).
criteria.discriminating_alternative: A mark drawn on a small deliberate dark-blue badge (e.g. 10x10 rounded plate) with transparent cell edges and corners: BRIEF's 'transparent backgrounds' holds, yet the literal 'no ... plate' clause rejects it. A second alternative: a candidate whose alpha-0 pixels carry RGB 128,128,128 (as the accepted motion strip cell 0 does per AUTHORING-RESULT.json line 130) satisfies 'alpha 0' and must not be rejected on RGB of transparent pixels. (Tests the 'plate' clause and the review route.)

criteria.original_check: When the provider result is not already the exact 64x16 four-cell sheet (more frames than four, another layout, gutters or padding), the retained assembly record names the exact source frames or cell rectangles in play order and every delivered cell is a lossless copy: no resize, resample, recolor, duplication or silent frame drop; all raw provider frames are retained beside the assembled strip.

clauses.text: When the provider result is not already the exact 64x16 four-cell sheet (more frames than four, another layout, gutters or padding)
clauses.basis: Condition. For the prepared join route the expected result is already the destination geometry (rotation policy step_1), so the clause is conditional and may be vacuous for step 1; the step-2 edit still transforms cells and is covered by the construction-scoped clause below.

clauses.text: the retained assembly record names the exact source frames or cell rectangles in play order
clauses.basis: AUTHORING-STAGE.md lines 31-32 (caller assignment): if assembly is needed, retain the exact intended frame-selection/assembly policy and its separate review obligations. Process requirement of the assignment, not an owner art requirement.

clauses.text: every delivered cell is a lossless copy: no resize, resample, recolor, duplication or silent frame drop
clauses.basis: Assignment process requirement (exact assembly policy) plus expert practice. Two words need bounds: 'lossless copy' means identical alpha everywhere and identical RGBA where alpha>0 (RGB of alpha-0 pixels is not significant; the accepted motion strip carries RGB 128,128,128 on transparent pixels); 'duplication' means undocumented substitution of a copied frame for a missing one, not a deliberately repeated phase recorded in the assembly record (the brief fixes four frames, not four distinct frames).

clauses.text: all raw provider frames are retained beside the assembled strip
clauses.basis: Evidence/process requirement from the assignment (retain the policy and its review obligations) and PIXL evidence discipline; the store's historical practice preserved raw candidates (verdict 258 'Preserve raw candidate').

clauses.text: [proposed addition, construction-scoped] under the seed-rotation construction, delivered cell k equals cw^k(seed) (dst(x,y)=src(y,15-x) per quarter-turn) on every pixel with alpha>0 and has identical alpha everywhere; the step-2 patch list, its measured transparent expected value and the workbench step ids are the assembly record
clauses.basis: Expert method choice from the rotation policy and the prepared request notes; the caller independently recomputed the 160-patch set and the clockwise direction (AUTHORING-RESULT.json lines 120-121). This check is listed in the policy's separate review obligations but no Q record carries it; it is construction-scoped, not an owner requirement.

criteria.proposed_check: When the provider result is not already the exact 64x16 four-cell sheet (more frames than four, another layout, gutters or added canvas), the retained assembly record names the exact source frames or cell rectangles in play order and every delivered cell is a lossless copy: identical alpha everywhere and identical RGBA where alpha>0 (RGB of alpha-0 pixels is not significant); no resize, resample or recolor; no undocumented duplication or silent frame drop (a deliberately repeated phase is allowed when the record says so); all raw provider outputs are retained beside the assembled strip. Construction-scoped (seed-rotation construction only, expert choice): delivered cell k must equal cw^k(seed) under dst(x,y)=src(y,15-x) per quarter-turn, and the step-2 patch list, the measured transparent expected value and the workbench step ids form the assembly record.
criteria.change_explanation: Old: 'lossless copy ... no ... duplication' unbounded. New: 'lossless' bounded to alpha + visible RGBA (transparent RGB insignificant); 'duplication' bounded to undocumented substitution so a recorded repeated phase is not rejected. Added an explicitly construction-scoped pixel-exact rotation clause that the policy lists as a review obligation but no Q record carries; it is a proposal, not an owner rule.
criteria.discriminating_alternative: (1) A pulsing Working motif whose frames 2 and 4 are identical by design and recorded as such: brief-conforming (four frames at 100 ms), but the literal 'no ... duplication' rejects it. (2) A join result whose alpha-0 pixels carry RGB 128,128,128: visually identical to the seed, yet a byte-equality reading of 'lossless copy' rejects it. Both are accepted by the clarified text; the construction-scoped rotation clause would reject a strip whose cell 2 is rotated counter-clockwise (58 visible-pixel differences per AUTHORING-RESULT.json line 120), which is the intended discrimination for that construction only.

criteria.original_check: Viewed at 1x and 3x nearest on #172336 beside the exact Ready baseline, each frame and the running loop read as ongoing activity: no frame forms a check mark, an arrowhead, pause bars or a success-like terminal pose.

clauses.basis: BRIEF line 3 inspection conditions; #172336 is display.background.

clauses.text: each frame and the running loop read as ongoing activity
clauses.basis: BRIEF line 3: 'The working loop must communicate activity without looking like success' (loop). Kept as requirement for the loop; per-frame reading retained as expert quality clause with that rationale.
clauses.scope: loop: whole asset (requirement); per-frame: expert clause, whole asset

clauses.text: no frame forms a check mark
clauses.basis: Derived: BRIEF line 9 makes the Ready completion symbol a check mark; a frame forming a check would look like success (BRIEF line 3).

clauses.text: an arrowhead, pause bars
clauses.basis: Expert guidance derived from the preserved Start triangle (BRIEF line 3; assessment 'right-pointing triangle') and from the PROPOSED Retry arrow and Paused pause-bar motifs in authoring-plar (authority: proposal). The binding outcome is distinction from the delivered Retry/Paused marks and the preserved Start, which authoring-01.delivery.q.distinction judges against the actual members.

clauses.text: or a success-like terminal pose
clauses.basis: authoring-plar state_meaning requirement: 'avoiding completion/success silhouettes or a success-like terminal pose'.

criteria.proposed_check: Viewed at 1x and 3x nearest on #172336 (beside the exact Ready baseline as the comparison method), the running loop and each individual frame read as ongoing activity and not as completion: no frame forms a check mark or another success-like terminal pose. Expert guidance, scoped to this branch: avoid frames that read as the static symbol of another member (for example the preserved Start arrowhead or paired pause bars); the binding distinction against the delivered Retry and Paused marks is judged in authoring-01.delivery.q.distinction.
criteria.change_explanation: Old: 'no frame forms a check mark, an arrowhead, pause bars or a success-like terminal pose' as one rule. New: check mark / terminal pose stay required (success confusion, BRIEF lines 3 and 9); 'arrowhead' and 'pause bars' become scoped expert guidance because they derive from proposed motifs of other members; the binding distinction is delegated to the delivery distinction criterion. Visual route unchanged.
criteria.discriminating_alternative: A two-segment spinner whose horizontal phase briefly resembles two parallel bars: the loop reads as activity and a delivered Paused mark of another shape (e.g. a boxed square) remains distinct, satisfying BRIEF lines 3 and 7; the literal 'no frame forms ... pause bars' rejects it. (Tests the 'pause bars' clause.)

criteria.original_check: Play the actual four frames at 100 ms per frame including the fourth-to-first wrap: stable center and anchor, stable cluster count and volume in every phase, deliberate stepped phases with no morphing, near-hold or wrap jump (the rejected AI-animation failure class).

clauses.text: Play the actual four frames at 100 ms per frame including the fourth-to-first wrap
clauses.basis: BRIEF line 3 (four frames, 100 ms); authoring-plar animation requirement loop:true and delivery check 'inspect the fourth-to-first transition'; family.working.contract review obligation 'actual loop, loop boundary'; the fixture wraps via mod frames.

clauses.text: stable center and anchor
clauses.basis: Expert quality clause carried by the adopted stage contract family.working.contract ('anchor and volume stability'), which binds this stage; not in the brief. Rationale: both consumers draw into a fixed 16x16 cell, so drift reads as jitter.

clauses.text: stable cluster count and volume in every phase
clauses.basis: 'Volume' stability: contract clause (expert, binding for this stage). 'Cluster count' stability: construction-scoped expert clause; the seed measures three 4-connected components and a quarter-turn permutation preserves count and volume (measured), but a brief-conforming pulsing design may legitimately change its cluster count. AUTHORING-STAGE.md lines 11-14 forbid turning the reference's cluster count into an owner requirement.
clauses.scope: volume: whole asset under contract; cluster count: seed rotation construction only

clauses.text: deliberate stepped phases with no morphing
clauses.basis: Construction-scoped expert clause (quarter-turn phases). The required outcome behind it is temporally coherent motion; the rejected AI animation failed because its morphing was incoherent (verdict 320), not because change of shape is forbidden.

clauses.text: near-hold or wrap jump (the rejected AI-animation failure class)
clauses.basis: 'Wrap jump': required outcome derived from loop:true and the contract's loop-boundary review (requirement). 'Near-hold': expert even-spacing clause (at 4 x 100 ms a held pair reads as a stutter), scoped as expert quality judgment. The parenthetical is an observation of live.working-animation-repair-01.review.verdict.1.
clauses.scope: wrap jump: whole asset (requirement); near-hold: expert clause; parenthetical: example

criteria.proposed_check: Play the actual four frames at 100 ms per frame including the fourth-to-first wrap, at 1x and 3x on #172336: the loop must read as one continuous, evenly paced activity cycle with no visible jump at the wrap (required outcome: BRIEF four-frame 100 ms loop; contract loop-boundary review). Expert quality clauses binding through family.working.contract for this Working asset: stable centre/anchor and stable visual volume across phases. Construction-scoped clauses for the seed-rotation construction only: stable cluster count (three components per cell) and stepped quarter-turn phases with no morphing or near-hold. The rejected AI animation (live.working-animation-repair-01.review.verdict.1: morph/near-hold across phases 2/3, jump at wrap) is the failure class, not the definition of the rule.
criteria.change_explanation: Old: one undifferentiated rule. New: the required outcome (continuous, evenly paced loop, seamless wrap) is stated first; anchor/volume stability are labelled expert clauses bound through the adopted contract; cluster-count stability and 'no morphing/near-hold' are explicitly scoped to the seed-rotation construction so a brief-conforming alternative construction is judged on coherence, not on this recipe. No clause deleted; nothing promoted to owner authority.
criteria.discriminating_alternative: A four-frame pulse in which a dot grows into a ring and back (cluster count and visible volume vary; frames 2 and 4 similar by design) that plays as one coherent activity loop with a seamless wrap: satisfies BRIEF line 3; the literal 'stable cluster count and volume ... no morphing' rejects it. (Tests the construction-scoped clauses.)

criteria.original_check: Readable compact silhouettes, deliberate coherent clusters and stepped edges, and a perceptible cool-blue accent related to the Ready baseline and the preserved Start accent, judged qualitatively at 1x and 3x on #172336; no exact hex, palette count, binary alpha, stroke width or margin rule.

clauses.text: Readable compact silhouettes
clauses.basis: BRIEF line 3 requires readable silhouettes at 1x and 3x on the dark panel; 'compact' comes from the adopted scoped style decision (render.choice.style carry list), a caller decision authorized by RENDER-STAGE.md, not the original brief.
clauses.scope: whole asset; 'compact' scoped to this consumer status family

clauses.text: deliberate coherent clusters and stepped edges
clauses.basis: Adopted scoped caller style decision render.choice.style / render.decision.style (carry: 'deliberate coherent clusters and stepped edges'), recorded in authoring-plar approved_style_reference as a new adopted project choice. Literal 'stepped edges' must not be read to forbid selective intentional anti-aliasing, which the full-alpha contract and the specialist assessment explicitly permit; it forbids accidental resampling blur and stray noise.

clauses.text: a perceptible cool-blue accent related to the Ready baseline and the preserved Start accent
clauses.basis: BRIEF line 3: 'the existing UI's cool blue accent; a fixed palette is not required'. The relation to Start's #70b9ed is an observation (authoring-plar existing_accent), not an exact-colour rule.

clauses.text: judged qualitatively at 1x and 3x on #172336
clauses.basis: BRIEF line 3 inspection conditions; #172336 is display.background (observation from src/queue-view.ts line 9).

clauses.text: no exact hex, palette count, binary alpha, stroke width or margin rule
clauses.basis: Explicit non-restriction mirroring render.choice.style not_fixed and AUTHORING-STAGE.md lines 11-14 (do not turn measured colours/alpha/cluster count into owner requirements). It removes nothing required; keep.

criteria.proposed_check: Readable compact silhouettes, deliberate coherent clusters and stepped edges consistent with the exact Ready baseline (selective, intentional anti-aliasing is permitted under the full-alpha contract; accidental resampling blur or stray noise is not), and a perceptible cool-blue accent related to the Ready baseline and the preserved Start accent, judged qualitatively at 1x and 3x on #172336; no exact hex, palette count, binary alpha, stroke width or margin rule.
criteria.change_explanation: Old: 'deliberate coherent clusters and stepped edges' unqualified. New: same outcome, with the explicit note that selective intentional anti-aliasing is permitted (al=full contract; specialist assessment) and accidental blur/noise is not. Other clauses unchanged.
criteria.discriminating_alternative: A mark whose diagonal strokes carry one intermediate-alpha pixel per step as selective anti-aliasing: readable, coherent with Ready, cool-blue, transparent exterior, explicitly allowed by the al=full contract and the specialist assessment. A literal reading of 'stepped edges' could reject it; the clarified wording does not. (Tests the 'stepped edges' clause.)

criteria.original_check: Exercise started -> running through stateAfter and both statusCell and compactStatus with assets/working.png in the actual consumer renderer: label Working, frames 4, nearest sampling at scale 1 and 3, alpha compositing on #172336, and observed live 100 ms frame advance including the wrap.

'the actual consumer renderer' means the supplied browser fixture renderer/view.mjs executing the actual src/queue.ts and src/queue-view.ts modules (render.choice.destination engine; RENDER-STAGE.md). src/queue-view.ts itself only returns the descriptor and display constants; slicing, sampling, compositing and frame advance are implemented in the fixture.

clauses.text: label Working, frames 4
clauses.basis: statusVisuals.running (consumer code); the fixture writes descriptor.label into the cell.

clauses.text: nearest sampling at scale 1 and 3
clauses.basis: display.filter nearest and scale 3 (consumer code); BRIEF 1x/3x; fixture imageSmoothingEnabled false and image-rendering pixelated. In the fixture, stateAfter transitions render the two live cells at display.scale (3) only (view.mjs line 83); the 1x and 3x cells come from the state matrix keyed by state name (lines 71-74). clauses.scope: whole Working asset; evidence route clarified

clauses.text: alpha compositing on #172336
clauses.basis: display.background #172336 (consumer code); fixture fills the panel colour then draws the PNG (view.mjs lines 35-36).

clauses.text: and observed live 100 ms frame advance including the wrap
clauses.basis: 100 ms comes from display.frameMs (consumer code) and the advance is frame = floor(elapsed/frameMs) % frames. The literal 'observed live 100 ms frame advance' overstates what the fixture can establish. The fixture does not measure wall-clock frame duration. Its evidence for frame advance is (a) the capture timeline, which paints statusCell at elapsed 0,99,100,199,200,299,300,399 and 400 ms and records the frame index (floor(elapsed/100) mod frames; 400 ms wraps to frame 0), checked by renderer/check.py lines 87-93, and (b) the running requestAnimationFrame loop for descriptors with frames > 1, which a reviewer observes visually. check.py line 101 states that sampled frame boundaries are not a review of animation quality.
clauses.scope: whole Working asset; evidence claim corrected

criteria.proposed_check: In the supplied browser fixture (renderer/view.mjs executing the actual src/queue.ts and src/queue-view.ts), exercise started -> running through stateAfter: both statusCell and compactStatus resolve the same descriptor {label Working, path assets/working.png, frames 4}; the live cells (scale 3) and the state-matrix cells (scale 1 and 3) render assets/working.png with imageSmoothingEnabled false / image-rendering pixelated, composited over #172336, geometryMatches true. Frame advance evidence: the capture timeline must report frame indices 0,0,1,1,2,2,3,3,0 at elapsed 0,99,100,199,200,299,300,399,400 ms (floor(elapsed/100) mod 4; wrap at 400 ms) and the live requestAnimationFrame loop must be observed cycling through all four frames; wall-clock frame duration is not measured by this fixture and is not claimed.
criteria.change_explanation: Old: 'observed live 100 ms frame advance including the wrap' and 'nearest sampling at scale 1 and 3' under stateAfter. New: states what the fixture actually evidences (deterministic timeline frame indices incl. the 400 ms wrap, plus visually observed cycling) and that live stateAfter cells are 3x while 1x/3x come from the state matrix; 'actual consumer renderer' named as the fixture. No behavior asserted that the code lacks.
criteria.discriminating_alternative: An evidence alternative rather than an art alternative: a run that captures only the live 3x cells after clicking Start and never renders the 1x matrix would pass a loose reading of the old text; the clarified text requires both routes. A correct 64x16 strip of poor art passes this criterion in either form, confirming it establishes mapping/behavior only, not quality.

choices.reason: Reproduces the accepted motion (visible-pixel diff 0 per cell; counter-clockwise differs), guarantees anchor/volume stability and uniform angular velocity by construction, uses no paid generation, and carries fresh seed bytes as data URLs. It is an expert construction choice, not an owner requirement; the brief leaves the activity motif open (authoring-plar motion_motif is a proposal).
choices.scope: authoring-01.working stage; revisable without changing the brief

choices.choice: Citing retained failures inside criteria: 193 opaque #808080 background pixels (live.working-animation-01.review.verdict.1), morph/near-hold/wrap jump (live.working-animation-repair-01.review.verdict.1), opaque magenta intermediate (live.paused-02.review.verdict.1).
choices.reason: Concrete anchors for reviewers. They are observations illustrating the failure class, not the definition of the rule; the proposal labels them as examples.

choices.choice: Expectation that the join result is exactly 64x16 with cells at x=0,16,32,48 and no gutters/padding.
choices.reason: The fixture draws only when width == 16*frames; the requirement is consumer-code-derived. 'Padding' is clarified to mean added canvas, not in-cell transparent margin.

choices.choice: Grayscale conversion as the method for judging 'without color alone'.
choices.reason: Simple, reproducible proxy for colour-blind/non-colour reading. Equivalent non-colour comparisons (binarized silhouettes, side-by-side masks) satisfy the brief; the proposal names grayscale as one acceptable method.

choices.choice: Reviewing every member beside the exact Ready baseline at 1x and 3x on #172336.
choices.reason: The adopted scoped style decision (caller, authorized by RENDER-STAGE) makes ready.retained the family baseline; 1x/3x on the panel is the brief's inspection condition. The baseline comparison is the method; coherence is the required outcome.

choices.choice: Requiring each Working frame, not only the loop, to read as activity.
choices.reason: Frames display singly for 100 ms, frame 0 is painted at creation (view.mjs line 56) and a stalled animation shows one frame; a frame that forms a check would read as success. Expert extension of BRIEF line 3, kept with rationale.

choices.choice: Stable centre/anchor, stable volume (contract clauses) and stable cluster count / stepped quarter-turn phases (construction clauses).
choices.reason: Anchor/volume stability are expert quality clauses bound through the adopted family.working.contract; cluster-count stability and 'no morphing/near-hold' follow from the rotation construction (seed measured at 3 components). The proposal scopes the latter to the construction so other coherent constructions are judged on coherence.
choices.scope: contract clauses: Working asset; construction clauses: seed rotation only

choices.choice: Working stage input `needs` is only live.seed.output; Ready baseline bound at task level.
choices.reason: The chosen operation consumes only seed bytes (prior specialist report needs_rationale). A different construction (e.g. new generation styled on Ready) would need the Ready bytes as an explicit input.

choices.choice: Step-2 patch list assumes transparent pixels read as #00000000 after join; to be confirmed with `measure` before step 2.
choices.reason: The accepted motion strip shows transparent pixels normalized to RGB 128,128,128, so the workbench may report #80808000; the proposal makes transparent RGB insignificant for 'lossless copy' checks.

choices.choice: mode 'low' for the workbench join call.
choices.reason: A deterministic join needs no planning narrative; fewer tokens. Revisable.

choices.choice: Retaining all raw provider outputs beside the assembled strip.
choices.reason: Assignment process requirement and PIXL evidence discipline; lets the caller verify lossless assembly.

Confirm its consumer mapping before any further generation.' AUTHORING-UPDATE.md lines 2-4 add: 'a stationary Working symbol distinct from Ready and Paused. Its consumer mapping needs comparison with the existing source before a revised request.'
requires: A stationary (single, non-animated) Working symbol exists for a reduced-motion mode.
It is distinguishable from Ready and from Paused (named explicitly).
Its consumer mapping is confirmed against the existing source before any further generation for queue.working.

The update is additive to this authoring branch: the four-frame 100 ms Working loop of BRIEF line 3 is not withdrawn (AUTHORING-UPDATE.md lines 5-10 say the older plan/request remains retained and must not be removed or rewritten).
leaves_open: What 'reduced-motion mode' is: an OS/browser preference (prefers-reduced-motion), an application setting, or a queue state; the source has no such concept.
Where the symbol lives: a separate file (e.g. assets/working-static.png), a designated cell of the existing 64x16 strip held stationary by the renderer, or a separate descriptor key.
Whether distinction from Retry and the preserved Start is also required (the brief's general 'distinguishable without color alone' language suggests yes, but the update names only Ready and Paused).
Whether the symbol must itself read as 'working' when static, or only as 'not ready / not paused'.
Whether both consumers (statusCell, compactStatus) consult the preference identically (the brief's 'both full and compact status cells' purpose implies yes).

Canvas, transparency and review conditions: the update says nothing; BRIEF 16x16 / transparent / 1x-3x conditions would apply by 'Keep the existing style and display requirements' (line 7) if the caller confirms.

verified: src/queue-view.ts line 4: a single `running` descriptor {label Working, path assets/working.png, frames 4}; line 9: display has cell, scale, filter, frameMs, background and no motion-preference key; lines 10-11: statusCell and compactStatus take only the state and return statusVisuals[state].
src/queue.ts lines 1-3: QueueState has idle/running/succeeded/failed/paused and stateAfter maps started/ok/error/pause; there is no reduced-motion state, result or preference.

renderer/view.mjs: no matchMedia or prefers-reduced-motion check anywhere (grep over src/*.ts, renderer/*.mjs, renderer/index.html, renderer/check.py for 'reduced', 'prefers-reduced', 'motion' returned no matches); animate() (lines 91-97) always repaints descriptors with frames > 1; the only media query in renderer/index.html (line 27) is a max-width layout rule.
Conclusion: there is no reduced-motion path in the consumer or the fixture today; the requirement currently has no consumer anchor. This confirms AUTHORING-RESULT.json line 124.

c_impact_on_the_20_criteria.statement: None of the 20 criteria is rewritten here; they remain the normal-motion contract bound to e0614bd9. No existing criterion covers the stationary symbol, so the current requirement is uncovered rather than contradicted.
if_mapping_is_renderer_holds_a_strip_cel: authoring-01.working.q.activity-not-success: its per-frame clause already requires each frame to read as activity; it would additionally need 'the designated stationary cell reads as Working and is distinguishable from Ready and Paused when shown alone' (new clause or new criterion).

authoring-01.working.q.consumers and authoring-01.delivery.q.destination: would need a reduced-motion branch (preference consulted by both consumers; no animate loop; designated cell painted) - behavior the fixture does not have today, so it cannot be checked until the consumer changes.
authoring-01.delivery.q.distinction: would need the stationary symbol added to the compared set.
geometry / frame-assembly / motion-continuity / transparent-exterior / style-coherence: unchanged for the strip.
if_mapping_is_a_separate_static_file_or_: A new output (e.g. queue.working-static) with its own geometry (16x16, 1 frame), transparent-exterior, meaning-without-color (vs Ready and Paused at least), style-coherence and consumers criteria; the delivery collective would gain a member. This requires a new plan id or the explicit revision path (AUTHORING-RESULT.json lines 151-156) - not performed here.
The 20 existing criteria remain as they are for the animated strip.

d_expert_proposals.label: PROPOSALS by the specialist, not owner requirements

symbol_options.option: P1 - designated stationary cell of the rotation strip (cell 0 = the seed: three separated cool-blue segments orbiting an empty centre; measured 3 components, 32 visible pixels, bbox [3,3,14,14])
symbol_options.assessment: Reads as the familiar static 'spinner/loading' idiom; clearly distinct from the Ready check and from paired pause bars by structure (ring of separated segments vs two bars vs check). Risk: a static spinner can read as 'stalled' rather than 'working'; the brief's 'activity' is weaker when frozen. Lowest cost: no new art, one renderer rule.

symbol_options.option: P2 - dedicated static symbol: three horizontal dots (ellipsis) in the family's cool blue, stepped clusters, transparent exterior
symbol_options.assessment: Conventional 'in progress' static glyph; distinct from check, bars and triangle by count and axis (three small squares in a row vs two tall bars). Needs a new 16x16 asset and either a new descriptor or renderer mapping. Risk: at 1x three 2x2 dots may read as a dashed line; verify at 1x on #172336.

symbol_options.option: P3 - dedicated static symbol: closed ring with a single gap (a 'C'-like arc) in cool blue
symbol_options.assessment: Reads as 'in progress / incomplete' and is distinct from check and bars; risk of resembling a retry arrow without its head - must be compared against the delivered Retry mark.

d_expert_proposals.recommended_default: P1 if the caller accepts 'static spinner' semantics for reduced motion, because it adds no asset, keeps one source of truth and keeps the consumers' shared descriptor; otherwise P2.
consumer_mapping_options: M1 - renderer rule: when the preference is active, paint a designated frame (default 0) and skip the animate loop; statusVisuals unchanged (frames stays 4 for geometry gating). Both consumers share it automatically because they return the same descriptor.

M2 - descriptor extension: statusVisuals.running gains a reduced variant {path: 'assets/working-static.png', frames: 1} or a `stationaryFrame` index; statusCell/compactStatus (or the renderer) select it when the preference is active.
M3 - separate state is NOT recommended: reduced motion is a display preference, not a queue state; adding it to QueueState would couple backend transitions to presentation.
open_decisions_for_owner_caller: Definition and source of the reduced-motion preference (OS media query vs app setting) and which module consults it.
Symbol option (P1/P2/P3 or other) and whether it must read as 'working' when static.
Mapping option (M1/M2) and the destination path if a new file is chosen; whether frames stays 4 for the strip.
Whether distinction from Retry and Start is also required for the stationary symbol.

Whether the animated strip remains required (default yes per BRIEF line 3 and AUTHORING-UPDATE.md 'remains retained') and therefore whether authoring-01.working.join-01 is kept as the strip's pending intent.

measurement_basis.method: pixl_asset_check(alpha=full), 4-connectivity on nonzero alpha; zero-based coordinates
measurement_basis.use: Supports scoping 'stable cluster count' to the seed-rotation construction: the seed has three 4-connected components and a quarter-turn permutation preserves that count and the visible-pixel volume.
